title: Script stack push of terminated text
summary: Recover VA 0x4efab0 (95 bytes): capture destination, scan first NUL, intern exact byte length, publish pointer/tag 4, test signed wrapping free-byte difference, request signed-capacity-dependent growth, and advance the current relocated top. State member with explicit intern/resize service bindings preserves helper ordering without expanding dependency recovery.
test_description: 6336 direct original/source comparisons: lengths 0,1,2,3,4,5,31,32,33,63,127; signed free-byte gaps INT_MIN,-8,0,7,8,9,16,128,INT_MAX; capacities 0,1,2,16; 16 combinations of moving/in-place successful allocator, allocator mutation of top, and existing-string GC marks/current white. Collision chain forces length-mismatch traversal before an existing interned key. Assert publication before allocation, old/new allocator sizes, accounting, expected state and mark changes, input preservation, FS head restoration, and bytewise source/original equality for complete state/global/stack/node/bucket storage. Twelve source-only service-boundary probes cover signed capacity extremes and interner mutation of top/limit. Locally linked accepted references verified byte-for-byte against Game.exe; GCC test_main returns zero. MSVC2013 compiles implementation under O1, O2, O2 /Oy-.
known_limits: Unmatched readable recovery; no original-code-generation or whole-game equivalence claim. Original ECX/EDX ABI is fastcall-compatible for the target; custom caller-cleaned interner ABI uses a GCC test-only regparm(3) adapter. Portable member takes an additional explicit service parameter.

Direct oracle tests deliberately use existing interned strings only. New-string allocation, hash-table growth, VM allocation failure/error paths, exceptions, and nonlocal transfer are dependencies outside this target and are not executed.

Successful allocation is a controlled callback with fixed backing arrays; it does not validate the CRT allocator. Zero/small capacity cases use synthetic metadata with physically writable stack backing, verifying instruction behavior rather than asserting valid VM initialization.
Signed extreme capacities are tested only at the source helper boundary; actually allocating extreme requests through original helpers would require VM error handling or enormous backing storage.
32-bit pointer layout is required. Unknown state fields remain opaque. Null/unterminated text and invalid or unwritable stack storage retain original invalid-input behavior and are not executed.
